To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hereditary bone tumors are a rare, heterogeneous group of disorders that can lead to multiple bone and soft tissue tumors and predispose to the occurrence of a variary of other malignant neoplasms.

1) the majority of hereditary bone tumors are caused by a single gene defect, 2) syndromes are often characterized by multiple benign and malignant neoplasms of various tissues and 3) syndromes can be recognized by the clinical phenotype, the time of tumor manifestation and the histological appearance of the tumor.
hereditary bone tumors are caused by germline mutations of tumor suppressor genes and predispose to the occurrence of multiple benign and malignant bone tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and clinical characterization of hereditary bone tumors and the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

the identification and analysis of the genetic and epigenetic basis for hereditary bone tumors, which is important in order to understand the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of bone tumors and to identify potential new targets for the treatment of bone tumors in general.
the molecular mechanisms of hereditary bone tumor syndromes and the development of novel treatment options.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hereditary bone tumors are a heterogeneous group of diseases, which can manifest as benign tumors or sarcomas.
the majority of hereditary bone tumor syndromes are not well understood.

a bone sarcoma in a patient with a known tumor predisposition syndrome should always be considered as a secondary manifestation of the underlying disease, whereas in a patient without a family history of tumors a bone sarcomas is a sporadic tumor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hereditary bone tumors are not as rare as once thought, but are still underdiagnosed.
we have to learn more about the molecular basis of hereditary bone tumors in order to better recognize and treat patients with hereditary tumors.
hereditary bone tumors are a rare entity, which can be recognized by their specific clinical, radiographic, histological and genetic features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recognition of the underlying genetic defect and the knowledge of the clinical manifestations are essential for the diagnosis, treatment and genetic counselling of patients and their relatives.
the recognition and early diagnosis of these syndromes can help to prevent or delay the onset of malignant bone tumors and to reduce the morbidity and mortality of these rare diseases.

the diagnosis of hereditary bone tumors is important, as early recognition of a syndrome and subsequent genetic testing can allow for early detection of other malignant tumors and the implementation of surveillance and prevention strategies.
